newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end up amid options-related volatility.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end up amid options-related volatility.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed higher amid volatile trade, shaking off early jitters after the government late Tuesday lost a key reform vote in Congress to rise ahead of Monday's options expiry, brokers said.
"The market was extremely nervous, but apparently there's interest in prices rising," a local trader said.
The Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index of 48 most-traded shares ended up 0.54 percent at 11,490 points on volume totalling 783.9 million reais ($725.8 million).
Brokers said the market was shaken early in the day after the Chamber of Deputies Tuesday night passed an amendment watering down President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's civil service reform bill.

Investors settled into a wait-and-see attitude later to await a vote tonight on the core of the legislation as well as a planned vote Thursday on a bill containing Brazil's new General Telecommunications Law, they said.
"If the government loses tonight, it will be a disaster, especially for foreigners who want badly to see these reforms passed," one local dealer said."
Trading remained highly volatile throughout Wednesday's session as players continued jostling for position ahead of next Monday's options settlements.
"The market will remain nervous probably until after futures settlements next Wednesday, June 18th. We may see some profit-taking after that," a local dealer said.
Much of the volatility was in benchmark Telebras preferred, which ended flat on heavy trade at 147.50 reais, while its common slipped 0.73 percent to end at 136.70 reais.
Among other major blue chips, mining giant Cia Vale do Rio Doce surged 5.26 percent to end at 279.99 reais, while state oil giant Petrobras dropped 3.09 percent to end at 157 reais.
Eletrobras' preferred B climbed 1.52 percent to end at 534 reais, helping to boost the bolsa's Electrical Energy Index 0.54 percent to a close of 3,113 points.
